text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R1", "statement": "queue_sms(household_id: str, template_id: str, params: dict, *, now=None) -> SmsMessage in notifications/sms.py queues one templated SMS to a household's registered phone number. It raises RuntimeError if feature('sms_enabled') is False and ValueError if the household has not agreed to receive SMS (household.sms_ok is False). It builds the message with SmsMessage(id=format_sms_id(next_number([m.id for m in sent_messages()], 'SMS-')), ...).", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "A SMS counts as SENT when a line is appended to data/outbox/sms.jsonl (store.append_jsonl). There is deliberately no function to edit or delete a line in an append-only file, so failed messages cannot be removed or edited — resending means appending new lines.", "file": "core/store.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "The SMS gateway records delivery results in data/sms_status.json as {\"SMS-00001\": \"delivered\", \"SMS-00002\": \"failed\", ...}. delivery_status() in notifications/sms.py returns this mapping; new messages have no entry yet. Failed messages can be identified as those with status == 'failed'.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "sent_messages() in notifications/sms.py returns [SmsMessage(**m) for m in store.read_jsonl(OUTBOX)] where OUTBOX = 'outbox/sms.jsonl'. SmsMessage (core/models.py) has fields: id, household_id, phone, template_id, params (dict, default {}), text (str, default ''), queued_at (str, default ''), and a to_dict() method (asdict).", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "SmsMessage IDs use format_sms_id(number) -> f\"SMS-{number:05d}\" (core/ids.py line 71-72), and next_number(existing_ids, prefix: str) -> int returns 1 + the highest number used so far with the prefix, so new resend IDs continue the SMS-NNNNN sequence.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "MAX_LENGTH == 140 and render(template_id, params) raises KeyError for unknown templates (e.g. 'FREE_TEXT') and ValueError if the rendered text exceeds 140 characters. TEMPLATES includes 'DELIVERY_DAY' (rendered with params site/day, starts with 'Lifeline:') and 'REVIEW' (no params).", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "Households are loaded via load_households(active_only=True) from registry/register.py; Household has sms_ok: bool = True (agreed to receive SMS) and a phone field. queue_sms uses the registered phone (m.phone == h.phone).", "file": "core/models.py"}, {"id": "R8", "statement": "Seed data has 8-10 failed SMS: test_every_seed_sms_has_a_delivery_status asserts {m.id for m in sent_messages()} == set(delivery_status()) and 8 <= sum(v == 'failed' for v in status.values()) <= 10. Every sent SMS has a delivery result, so failed IDs can be matched back to sent_messages() entries.", "file": "tests/test_notifications.py"}, {"id": "R9", "statement": "Ops scripts live in scripts/ and must insert the repo root into sys.path (sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))) before importing project modules. Scripts that send payments or SMS, or change data/registry.json or data/ledger.json, must say so in their docstring.", "file": "scripts/stock_report.py"}, {"id": "R10", "statement": "To resend with the same message and details as the original, the script can read the original SmsMessage from sent_messages() and re-queue via queue_sms(m.household_id, m.template_id, m.params) — this re-renders the same text and uses the household's registered phone. Note queue_sms checks sms_ok at send time, so a household that opted out since the original send would raise ValueError and be skipped.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}]}}
